clues.q: Playback singers record the songs that actors lip-sync on screen in this Mumbai-based Hindi film industry.
This nine-member K-pop girl group had hits with “What Is Love?” in 2018 and “Fancy” in 2019.
This Filipino singer won a 1991 Tony Award as Kim in “Miss Saigon” and later sang for Disney’s Princess Jasmine.
This Indonesian instrument of tuned bamboo tubes, sounded by shaking it, is on UNESCO’s intangible heritage list.
The oud, central to Arab, Persian, and Turkish music, is what kind of instrument?
This 1998 Disney animated film follows a young woman who takes her father’s place in the Chinese army.
In Pixar’s 2022 film “Turning Red,” 13-year-old Mei Lee transforms into this fluffy animal when she gets excited.
Dev Patel plays Saroo, an Indian-born man raised in Australia who uses Google Earth to find his birth family, in this 2016 film.
This 2017 Thai thriller follows a brilliant student who runs an elaborate exam-cheating scheme for classmates.
Stephen Chow directed and starred in this 2004 Hong Kong action comedy set in a run-down housing complex called Pigsty Alley.
Ancient Mesopotamia, the land between the Tigris and Euphrates, lies mostly within this modern country.
The sage Laozi is traditionally credited as the founder of this Chinese philosophy and religion.
The ruins of ancient Troy, made famous by Homer’s “Iliad,” lie in this modern country.
These seafaring people of the ancient Levant, based in cities like Tyre and Sidon, created an alphabet that inspired the Greek one.
Named for a village in northern Vietnam, this Bronze Age people are famous for their large, intricately decorated bronze drums.
clues.a: What is the Đông Sơn culture?

clues.q: In 2018, the Winter Olympics were held in PyeongChang in this country.
In 1984, this small oil-rich sultanate on the island of Borneo became fully independent from Britain.
This federation that includes Abu Dhabi and Dubai was formed in 1971.
clues.a: What is the United Arab Emirates?

clues.q: In 1953, this Sherpa and Edmund Hillary became the first confirmed climbers to reach the summit of Everest.
In 1997, Kazakhstan moved its capital to Astana from this largest city in the country’s southeast.
This country’s flag is red with a single yellow five-pointed star in the center.
The gold-covered Shwedagon Pagoda towers over the city of Yangon in this country.
Home to Jakarta and Yogyakarta, this Indonesian island is the most populous island in the world.
This Malaysian state on northern Borneo is home to Mount Kinabalu.
Seat of the Nguyễn dynasty, this former imperial capital of Vietnam sits on the Perfume River.
These chewy Japanese rice cakes are often filled with sweet red bean paste.
This Indian dessert of deep-fried milk-dough balls is soaked in sugar syrup often scented with rosewater or cardamom.
Called lokum in Turkey, this soft gel candy is often flavored with rosewater and dusted with powdered sugar.
Ube, which gives many Filipino desserts their vivid purple color, is a kind of this starchy root vegetable.
This Thai dessert, khao niao mamuang, pairs coconut-sweetened glutinous rice with slices of a ripe yellow fruit.

clues.q: Often called Korea’s unofficial national anthem, this beloved folk song exists in thousands of regional versions.
clues.hint: Its refrain names a mountain pass.

clues.q: This style of Japanese ensemble drumming features huge drums struck with sticks called bachi.
clues.hint: Often performed at festivals with dramatic, athletic movements.

clues.q: In this Korean musical storytelling tradition, a single singer performs for hours accompanied by one drummer.
clues.hint: The singer often holds a folding fan as a prop.

clues.q: The son of Alla Rakha, this Indian percussionist became the world’s most famous tabla virtuoso.
clues.hint: He co-founded the fusion band Shakti with John McLaughlin.

clues.q: This Mongolian band went viral in 2018 and 2019 by blending heavy rock with throat singing and the horsehead fiddle.
clues.hint: Songs include “Wolf Totem” and “Yuve Yuve Yu.”

clues.q: Jackie Chan plays Mr. Han, a maintenance man who teaches kung fu to Jaden Smith, in this 2010 remake.
clues.hint: The 1984 original starred Ralph Macchio.

clues.q: This anime follows Tanjiro Kamado, who joins a corps of swordsmen hoping to cure his sister Nezuko.
clues.hint: Its full title adds “Kimetsu no Yaiba.”

clues.q: Aamir Khan plays Rancho, a free-spirited engineering student, in this 2009 Bollywood comedy.
clues.hint: Its catchphrase is “All is well.”

clues.q: Hirokazu Kore-eda’s 2018 film about a makeshift family that steals to get by won the Palme d’Or.
clues.hint: The boy Shota learns to pocket goods from his “father” Osamu.

clues.q: Apichatpong Weerasethakul won the 2010 Palme d’Or for this Thai film about a dying man visited by ghosts.
clues.a: What is Uncle Boonmee Who Can Recall His Past Lives?
clues.hint: The title character remembers earlier incarnations.

clues.q: Han dynasty official Cai Lun is traditionally credited with inventing this writing material.
clues.hint: Before it, people wrote on bamboo strips and silk.

clues.q: Queen Zenobia ruled from this wealthy caravan city in the Syrian desert.
clues.hint: Its ruins include the great Temple of Bel.

clues.q: Named for its giant keyhole-shaped burial mounds, this period of early Japanese history ran from about 300 to 538 CE.
clues.hint: It followed the Yayoi period.

clues.q: The library of King Ashurbanipal, which preserved tablets of the Epic of Gilgamesh, stood in this Assyrian capital.
clues.hint: Its ruins face the modern city of Mosul across the Tigris.

clues.q: This 12th-century Khmer king commissioned Angkor Wat.
clues.hint: His name begins with “Surya,” the Hindu sun god.

clues.q: In 1960, Sirimavo Bandaranaike of Ceylon became the world’s first woman to hold this office.
clues.hint: The same office Nehru held in India.

clues.q: In 2018, twelve boys from a youth soccer team and their coach were rescued from this flooded cave in northern Thailand.
clues.hint: The team was called the Wild Boars.

clues.q: In what year did Dubai’s Burj Khalifa officially open?
clues.hint: The same year Shanghai hosted the World Expo.

clues.q: This Indian space agency was founded on August 15, 1969.
clues.hint: Its Chandrayaan-3 landed near the Moon’s south pole in 2023.

clues.q: In 1998, Hong Kong’s new international airport opened on this island.
clues.hint: It replaced Kai Tak, known for its hair-raising landings.

clues.q: This Venetian merchant described the court of Kublai Khan in a famous travel book.
clues.hint: A swimming-pool game is named after him.

clues.q: Its larvae feed on mulberry leaves and spin the cocoons used for China’s most famous fabric.
clues.hint: Its scientific name is Bombyx mori.

clues.q: This Moroccan traveler of the 1300s journeyed through Central Asia, India, and China.
clues.hint: He dictated his adventures in a book called the Rihla.

clues.q: This Uzbek city, home to the Ark fortress and the Kalyan Minaret, was a great Silk Road center.
clues.hint: A style of red patterned rug shares its name.

clues.q: These walled roadside inns gave Silk Road traders and their camels shelter for the night.
clues.hint: Persia’s Shah Abbas I built many of them.

clues.q: This island in the Andaman Sea is Thailand’s largest.
clues.hint: Patong Beach is its nightlife hub.

clues.q: The Chocolate Hills are the top attraction on this Philippine island province.
clues.hint: Also known for tiny, big-eyed tarsiers.

clues.q: This Malaysian island in the Strait of Malacca has George Town as its capital.
clues.hint: Famous for char kway teow and other hawker food.

clues.q: This southern Japanese island prefecture was once the Ryukyu Kingdom.
clues.hint: Its capital is Naha.

clues.q: This oddly shaped Indonesian island, with four long peninsulas, is home to the port city of Makassar.
clues.hint: Europeans once called it Celebes.

questions.q: Which of these countries has a coastline?
Name the long draped garment worn by many women in India.
Southeast Asia’s durian fruit is famous for its strong…
Name the traditional Japanese robe worn with a wide obi sash.
The Kathakali dance-drama comes from which Indian state?
Name the woven straw mats used as flooring in traditional Japanese rooms.

rounds.name: Final Round
rounds.q: This UNESCO-listed bay in Quảng Ninh province, northern Vietnam, is dotted with some 1,600 limestone islands and islets.
rounds.hint: Junk-boat cruises depart from nearby Bãi Cháy.

clues.q: This end-blown Japanese bamboo flute was once played by wandering Zen monks.
clues.hint: Monks of the Fuke sect played it wearing basket-like hats.

clues.q: This Vietnamese instrument has just one string and is played using harmonics.
clues.hint: The pitch is bent with a flexible rod at one end.

clues.q: This classical music tradition of South India is closely associated with the composer Tyagaraja.
clues.hint: Its northern counterpart is Hindustani music.

clues.q: This two-stringed, long-necked lute is Kazakhstan’s national instrument.
clues.hint: Kurmangazy composed famous pieces for it.

clues.q: Played on a row of small gongs laid on a wooden frame, this ensemble music is a tradition of Mindanao in the Philippines.
clues.hint: The gongs are laid horizontally, bosses facing up.

clues.q: In this 2016 Makoto Shinkai anime hit, a Tokyo boy and a country girl mysteriously swap bodies.
clues.hint: A comet plays a crucial role.

clues.q: Bong Joon Ho’s 2013 English-language film is set on a train endlessly circling a frozen Earth.
clues.hint: Chris Evans leads a revolt from the tail section.

clues.q: This Iranian director won the 1997 Palme d’Or for “Taste of Cherry.”
clues.hint: He also made “Close-Up” and the Koker trilogy.

clues.q: Wong Kar-wai’s 1994 film tells two stories of lovelorn Hong Kong policemen.
clues.hint: Faye Wong’s character plays “California Dreamin’” on repeat.

clues.q: Lino Brocka’s 1975 classic follows a young fisherman searching for his lost love in the Philippine capital.
clues.a: What is Manila in the Claws of Light?
clues.hint: Often ranked the greatest Filipino film ever made.

clues.q: This Bronze Age empire of Anatolia, with its capital at Hattusa, rivaled Egypt.
clues.hint: They fought Ramesses II at the Battle of Kadesh.

clues.q: Founded by Liu Bang after the fall of the Qin, this ruling house gave its name to China’s largest ethnic group.
clues.hint: It ruled for about four centuries, split into Western and Eastern halves.

clues.q: This Tamil dynasty’s king Rajaraja I built the great Brihadeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur.
clues.hint: Its navy raided Srivijaya in the 11th century.

clues.q: This early kingdom of the lower Mekong, described by Chinese chroniclers, had a major trading port at Óc Eo.
clues.hint: It was later overtaken by Chenla.

clues.q: Founded around 1046 BCE, this Chinese ruling house developed the idea of the Mandate of Heaven.
clues.hint: It overthrew the Shang.

clues.q: Sukarno and Hatta proclaimed Indonesia’s independence on August 17 of this year.
clues.hint: The same year World War II ended.

clues.q: In 1983, this Kyoto-based company released the Family Computer, or Famicom.
clues.hint: Western gamers knew the console as the NES.

clues.q: In 1971, this Persian Gulf island nation became independent from Britain.
clues.hint: The King Fahd Causeway links it to Saudi Arabia.

clues.q: Which city hosted the 1998 Winter Olympics?
clues.hint: A Japanese city known for Zenkō-ji temple.

clues.q: When North and South Yemen unified in 1990, this city became the capital.
clues.hint: Its old city is famous for decorated multistory tower houses.

clues.q: In 1961, this cosmonaut became the first human in space, launching from Baikonur in Kazakhstan.
clues.hint: His spacecraft was Vostok 1.

clues.q: Nicknamed the “Roof of the World,” this mountain range lies mostly in Tajikistan.
clues.hint: The M41 highway across them is famous with adventure cyclists.

clues.q: This large Kyrgyz lake in the Tian Shan rarely freezes despite sitting about 1,600 meters above sea level.
clues.hint: Cholpon-Ata is the main resort on its north shore.

clues.q: This burning gas crater in Turkmenistan’s Karakum Desert is nicknamed the “Door to Hell.”
clues.hint: It lies along the road north from Ashgabat.

clues.q: This 15th-century Timurid ruler and astronomer built a great observatory and compiled a famous star catalogue.
clues.hint: He was Timur’s grandson.

clues.q: This Japanese author wrote “Norwegian Wood” and “Kafka on the Shore.”
clues.hint: He also wrote “1Q84.”

clues.q: This 13th-century Persian poet, who lived in Konya, inspired the Mevlevi order of whirling dervishes.
clues.hint: His masterpiece is the Masnavi.

clues.q: In 1913, this Bengali poet became the first Asian to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.
clues.hint: He won for the poetry collection “Gitanjali.”

clues.q: José Rizal’s 1887 novel exposed abuses under Spanish rule in the Philippines.
clues.hint: Its sequel is “El Filibusterismo.”

clues.q: Attributed to Luo Guanzhong, this classic Chinese novel follows the rival warlords Liu Bei, Cao Cao, and Sun Quan.
clues.a: What is Romance of the Three Kingdoms?
clues.hint: Zhuge Liang is its master strategist.

questions.q: Capital of Oman?
questions.hint: Shares its name with a grape variety.

questions.q: Capital of Lebanon?
questions.hint: A Mediterranean port once called the “Paris of the Middle East.”

questions.q: Capital of Azerbaijan?
questions.hint: On the Caspian Sea, famous for its Flame Towers.

questions.q: Capital of Timor-Leste?
questions.hint: Four letters, starts with D.

questions.q: Largest city of Sri Lanka?
questions.hint: Its Galle Face Green promenade faces the Indian Ocean.

questions.q: Capital of the Maldives?
questions.hint: Four letters, starts with M.

questions.q: Currency of Laos?
questions.hint: Three letters, starts with K.

questions.q: Currency of Myanmar?
questions.hint: Four letters, starts with K.

questions.q: Currency of Kazakhstan?
questions.hint: Five letters, starts with T.

questions.q: Indonesian or Malay for “thank you”?
questions.hint: Two words; the first begins with T.

questions.q: Malay word for “person,” found in the name of a great ape?
questions.hint: The ape lives on Borneo and Sumatra.

questions.q: Poet who wrote Iran’s national epic, the Shahnameh?
questions.hint: He lived around 1000 CE in Tus, near Mashhad.

questions.q: Strait that divides Istanbul between Europe and Asia?
questions.hint: It links the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara.

questions.q: Vietnamese Lunar New Year?
questions.hint: Children receive lucky money called lì xì.

questions.q: Persian New Year, celebrated at the spring equinox?
questions.hint: Families set a haft-sin table of seven symbolic items.

questions.q: Istanbul’s Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) was built under which empire?
questions.hint: Founded by Osman I around 1300.

questions.q: Name the Mughal emperor, Babur’s grandson, who built the city of Fatehpur Sikri.
questions.hint: His son and successor was Jahangir.

questions.q: In the Ramayana, Rama rescues Sita from which island kingdom?
questions.hint: It was ruled by the ten-headed Ravana.

questions.q: Name the Thai national epic, a version of the Ramayana.
questions.hint: Its murals line the galleries of Bangkok’s Wat Phra Kaew.

questions.q: The Registan, a square framed by three grand madrasas, is in which city?
questions.hint: It was Timur’s capital.

questions.q: Name the 17th-century Japanese haiku master who wrote “The Narrow Road to the Deep North.”
questions.hint: He spent his later years traveling on foot across Japan.

rounds.name: Hard Final
rounds.q: Born near Bukhara around 980, this Persian polymath wrote “The Canon of Medicine,” a standard medical text in Europe for centuries.
rounds.hint: He also wrote “The Book of Healing,” a vast work of philosophy and science.
